question_text: A 31-year-old G3P2 woman presents to labor and delivery triage because she has had bleeding over the last day. Physical exam reveals an alert woman with slow, painless, vaginal bleeding. Which of the following risk factors are associated with the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

                    ### Question
                    A 31-year-old G3P2 woman presents to labor and delivery triage because she has had bleeding over the last day. She is currently 5 months into her pregnancy and has had no concerns prior to this visit. She previously had a delivery through cesarean section and has otherwise had uncomplicated pregnancies. She denies fever, pain, and discomfort. On presentation, her temperature is 99.1°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, pulse is 81/min, and respirations are 15/min. Physical exam reveals an alert woman with slow, painless, vaginal bleeding. Which of the following risk factors are associated with the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Early menarche
opb. Multiparity
opc. Presence of uterine fibroids
opd. Pelvic inflammatory disease
ope. Smoking

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Multiparity and presence of uterine fibroids are associated with an increased risk of placental abnormalities such as placenta previa and placental abruption, leading to vaginal bleeding in pregnancy. Smoking is also linked to an increased risk of placental abruption. Considering the patient's symptoms of painless vaginal bleeding, the most likely cause could be related to placental abnormalities associated with multiparity or uterine fibroids.
